cluster_name: North Korea fires ballistic missile amid DMZ landmine row with Seoul
tldr: All 13 headlines foreground the ballistic missile launch itself; roughly half additionally embed the causal trigger — Seoul's apology demand over the DMZ mine blast, or Kim Yo-jong's rejection of dialogue — collapsing the story into a clean action-reaction frame at the homepage level. Technical detail (flight distance, EEZ exposure, Seoul-Washington joint tracking) visible in body texts is entirely suppressed across every headline in the corpus.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline in the corpus to name Kim Yo-jong's explicit rejection of dialogue as the direct trigger, foregrounding the diplomatic breakdown rather than the missile flight alone.

Uses 'unidentified projectile' rather than 'ballistic missile' in one headline — the most hedged attribution in the corpus, signalling that South Korea's national wire had not yet confirmed missile type at time of publication.

Carries a late-September 'suspected ballistic missiles toward East Sea: JCS' headline in addition to the Oct 3 launch, the only outlet whose headline layer establishes this as a second launch event rather than an isolated incident.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, North Korea's missile launch is universally framed as a security event; roughly half the corpus also embeds the political trigger (Seoul's apology demand or Kim Yo-jong's dialogue rejection), but technical detail and alliance-coordination content visible in body texts are entirely absent from all 13 headlines.
